scope: French and Arabic source research for two unresolved historical project entries; website identity verification only. No numerical score, uptime conclusion or assertion that no website exists.
method: Check dated primary institutional announcements and the official gazette.
Trace agency and government-directory links; distinguish historical labels from current endorsements.
Separate search-index content, direct retrieval and independent ownership evidence.
Exclude shared ministry hosts and similarly named institutions from substitute scoring.
limitations: Search results are not exhaustive proof of absence.
Indexed candidate content can be stale or self-asserted.
Collector retrieval and DNS failures are not website availability measurements.
No contact form, email or private system was used to request confirmation.

entries.note: The Mines portfolio is confirmed, but no current dedicated official website was independently established. mm.edihosts.com is a credible historical candidate with indexed 2026 updates, rather than a proven commercial preview. Its current authorization remains unverified. oilmines.gov.dz now identifies itself as Hydrocarbons and is not substituted for Mines.

findings.finding: National public radio reports Mourad Hanifi taking office as minister of Mines and Mining Industries. This verifies the portfolio and officeholder at that date, not a dedicated domain.
The ministry explicitly announces renaming its official platforms to Ministry of Hydrocarbons. The legacy page title and remaining Mines navigation do not establish a separate Mines website.

entries.institutionStatus: Presidential inspection body confirmed by primary historical text; current ministerial representation requires revalidation
entries.note: The presidential State Services and Local Authorities Inspectorate is identifiable, but a dedicated public website remains unverified. APS reports Brahim Merad moving to Interior on 13 October 2026. That change does not establish dissolution or a successor. Presidency, mediator and other ministries’ inspection pages are not substituted.

findings.accessMode: Official PDF and independently retrieved search-index text; the PDF text extractor did not find the decree string
findings.finding: The text identifies the General Inspectorate of State Services and Local Authorities as an inspection body under the authority of the President. This distinguishes it from sectoral inspectorates and does not by itself establish its current website.

APS relays the presidential announcement appointing Brahim Merad to Interior and Local Authorities. An older entry naming him inspectorate minister is insufficient for current portfolio verification. The announcement does not prove that the inspection body was abolished.
The same-day presidential reception report describes Merad in the inspectorate role before his Interior appointment. This corroborates the identity transition, not a dedicated website.
The directory links the Presidency and mediator as separate institutions. Neither is evidence of a dedicated inspectorate website.
This page describes Justice-sector inspectorates, so it is excluded as an identity mismatch.

candidates.decision: Parent Presidency host, not established as a dedicated inspectorate website; research-tool timeout is not an outage conclusion.

entries.currentScopeCaveat: The 34-entry project corpus is historical. A change in officeholder does not justify deleting this entry or claiming the exact current cabinet composition.
